item.content:encoded:

I guess I'll explain what I can about the narrative; I wasn't going to, since this is only a brief initial pitch, but hopefully you'll find this to be interesting at least.

If you want greenlights on an idea, you have to pitch the whole idea and not just some of it.

My concern with the narrative here is that it feels…lacking in closure? It might work if you can get a reader to feel invested in the SCP and so it being frozen indefinitely ends up feeling like a huge sad moment; but it feels like it might be hard to land that in a way that works? Particularly since the freezing here is implied to be perfect (i.e., that they've circumvented the usual issues where ice shards form within a body and rupture the cells); and so in turn, there's an implication that even if they wait a really long time, they could still wake her up?

The other issue with doing a sad ending here is that it feels like it might be really hard to get a reader to emphasise with the legs here; like…it's not like they can really talk and be a character and so you're likely going to have to rely on characterising them via their actions and mannerisms.


I'm willing to greenlight this though because I don't think either thing here is a major issue, and I think it'll be easier to tell if it works via a draft y'know? This said: there's a possibility this might work best as a tale and I'd urge you to seriously consider that. It'd allow you to spend a lot more time in the researchers mind if this was like…a write up of that investigation happening and his reaction to stuff, than if like, he has to formally write it up in a SCP file, y'know?

item.title: Re: Greenlight request- Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.content:encoded:
I guess I'll explain what I can about the narrative; I wasn't going to, since this is only a brief initial pitch, but hopefully you'll find this to be interesting at least. Here's the plot summary:

+ show block
– hide block

I'm hoping that the reader will interpret that by the absence of fetal tissue in the enlarged uterus and the shrunken portions of the woman's brain that regulate cognitive functions, sensory input, movement, and memory, that the fetus mutated in a way that caused it to absorb the mother's brain functions and dissolve, sinking into the legs with only the nervous system surviving, which means that the nervous system is essentially a hive mind of the mother and fetus. The mother had been wandering as a result of her brain's degradation and died in the snow, being frozen for an indiscriminate amount of time so that it would be difficult to pinpoint when she died. When the corpse thawed, the legs and lower torso forcibly pulled itself away from the upper body, confused due to its overall lack of "brain power," but with enough sense of direction (likely due to the mutation, or perhaps from the mother's prior knowledge and memory) to know approximately where the nearest village is, but never finds its way there and is instead picked up by the foundation when villagers report seeing it in the distance. It returns to the top half of the corpse before being acquired. The information that helps the reader determine this is revealed in different segments in the description section.

The scientist's observation session, which he commentates for the audio file, involves the scientist explaining that in the last two sessions, it had tried to exit the lab, so for this one, he has evacuated and disinfected the halls to observe what the skip does when it's let out. It blindly but frantically crawls along walls, feeling each doorway before coming to the facility's north exit and being adamant about trying to move through the exit, likely because it can sense the air coming from the outside. After failing to open the door by kicking it, it quickly scurries back to the freezer unit it's kept in and huddles back against its top half, connecting with it like a puzzle piece. As the scientist ends the session and closes the freezer, he hesitates, thinking he saw the top half's arm move, but dismisses it as a trick of light from the leg twitching. As he closes it, a raspy voice whispering, "Need Dad," can be briefly heard as the door is closing (this is not included in the transcript, only the audio file). Since the entity is likely a hive mind, the reader is left to interpret that it is looking for a specific family member, either the baby's father or the mother's father, who probably lived in the village where it was found. The reader will hopefully interpret that the skip was able to transfer some of its neurons to the top half to briefly control the mouth and vocal cords, and when the skip was initially acquired in two pieces, it was probably attempting to do the same thing. So it longs for closure.

The scientist doesn't hear the voice coming from the top half and dismisses the session as only partly informative about what it can do. He keeps the skip frozen to preserve its lifespan until it can be determined if this was a single mutation or something contagious that can happen again. A second addendum reveals that some researchers who listened to the scientist's recording noticed the indiscriminate sound as he closed the door, but the scientist has failed in his attempts to recreate the circumstances that allowed the whisper to be heard. He dismisses it as a noise that he perhaps made involuntarily as he closed the freezer door, thus dooming the skip to be frozen indefinitely.

I hope this is enough to constitute a beginning, middle, and end for a narrative. If you don't agree or don't find it interesting, let me know.

item.title: Greenlight request- Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.content:encoded:
I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror (body horror)

Page Layout (Optional): Class, containment procedures, description, addenda (including a voiceover mp3 file with sound effects)

Elevator Pitch: Pregnant woman is found frozen in the arctic, torn in half, fetus missing. Top half of body is dead, lower half moves erratically on its own, possibly with a purpose or cognition.

Central Narrative: Corpse was found frozen in Yukon when villagers noticed a strange, unidentified creature moving erratically. Corpse's lower half is controlled by a series of live neurons that consume the bone and ligament tissue and shock the muscles into moving convulsively, allowing it to crawl. It will violently hyperextend its joints (bending knees backwards and such) and break its own bones to move.

+ show block
– hide block

The live neuron DNA matches the dead woman, whose brain is somewhat shrunken, or possibly her fetus. Lead scientist believes it's capable of navigation and is searching for something, but regrets that its lifespan is so short as a result of consuming its own flesh and progressively deflating in size, that they'll never know what it wants. It must remain frozen to stay alive until the foundation finds a way to save it or find what it's looking for.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Using body horror as a focus, of which I haven't seen much here, and a full story with open-ended conclusion that is coherent with beginning, middle, and end if the reader reads between the lines. Specifically, I'd like to include a voiceover file from the scientist's observation session with written transcript, recording the skittering and cracking noises the skip makes, with a subtle hint/easter egg for readers to listen for, revealing what it's capable of, and possibly answering the question of what it actually wants (this won't be included in the transcript, so that the reader is left to think and interpret it on their own).

Additional Notes: Please advise how to include the mp3 file with submission, as it's essential to the storytelling, thanks.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
